tools.name: run_test
tools.description: Start a Menso test on a live website. An AI user with a realistic persona opens the site in a real cloud browser and tries to complete a task; Menso then scores the run (TRACES, 0-100) and records where the user got stuck, with a replay of every step. Templates: 'purchase' (default) reads the homepa

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Check a Menso test started with run_test. state is one of: queued, running (with step progress), paused (the AI user is waiting for you in the Menso web app, e.g. for a verification code), scoring (the AI user finished and Menso is scoring the run), done (call get_findings), failed, or stopped. Poll

tools.name: get_findings
tools.description: Get the results of a finished Menso test: the TRACES score (0-100) with each dimension's 0-5 score and reason, and the task outcome. tools.name: get_replay_link
tools.description: Create, or return the existing, public replay link for a finished Menso test: a menso.io/r/... page that shows every step the AI user took and what they thought. Anyone with the link can watch it, so share it deliberately. Included in the Pro and Studio plans; on Free it returns an upgrade note inst

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "run_test" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_findings · Private data: run_test · Public sink: run_test, get_replay_link · Destructive: run_test, get_status, get_findings.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_findings · Private data: run_test · Public sink: run_test, get_replay_link · Destructive: run_test, get_status, get_findings

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
